message: docs(agents): carry the read-back rule, and decode the manifest fatally in readStore (#478)

edits.find: A checkpoint is the route when the work is a stack.
edits.replace:
**A write is not done until its blob id is read back.** After every contents-API write, compare the `content.sha` in the response with the Git blob id declared for that path before the write. A mismatch stops the push: do not write the next file, do not push the manifest, and do not report success. Re-write the file and compare again. Before pushing a manifest, list the store directory at the branch head and confirm every patch's blob id and size equal the plan. `push_files` returns no per-file blob id, so transport checkpoint files with `create_or_update_file`, one file per call. The lines a transcriber normalises are the ones to watch: a line that is exactly one space, which is every blank context line of a unified diff, the line after a hunk header, trailing whitespace, the final line and its LF, backtick spans, and non-ASCII. [ADR-104](docs/ADR-104-a-transport-write-is-read-back-before-it-counts.md) records why this is a rule rather than a serializer.

With a runtime, `node scripts/checkpoint-transport.mjs plan <store-dir>` prints every store file in push order with its size, blob id, SHA-256 and a numbered map of those lines; print it outside the repository, since a stray file under `.ai/checkpoints/` refuses every later checkpoint. `node scripts/checkpoint-transport.mjs verify <store-dir> <path>=<blob-id>...` compares observed ids with the plan and exits non-zero unless every patch matches and nothing stray is stored, and `localize <expected-file> <observed-file>` names the first differing line. The helper is first-party and lives in `scripts/` with its cases; `.tools/` holds only the retained Prettier archive, and no helper belongs there.

A checkpoint is the route when the work is a stack.
